transcript.text: roomba e5 wont charge properly, sometimes it does sometimes it doesnt

Intermittent charging on a Roomba e5 is usually caused by dirty/poorly aligned charging contacts, a weak Home Base power supply, or an aging battery.

One important note: on the e5, the charging light may turn off after about a minute to conserve power even while it is still charging. Press CLEAN once or check the iRobot Home app to confirm its battery/charging status.

Try this in order:

1. Clean all charging contacts
• Unplug the Home Base.
• Wipe the two metal contacts on the bottom of the Roomba and the two spring contacts on the dock.
• Use a dry microfiber cloth; if they are oxidized/grimy, use a small amount of isopropyl alcohol on the cloth, then let everything dry fully.
• Make sure the dock’s spring-loaded contacts move freely and are not stuck down.

2. Check how it sits on the dock
• Put the dock on a hard, level floor—not thick carpet.
• Ensure the robot is centered and that both metal pads touch the dock contacts.
• With the Roomba docked, gently press it down/back toward the dock. If charging starts only when you do that, it is a contact/alignment issue.

3. Check dock power
• Plug the Home Base directly into a known-good wall outlet, bypassing power strips or surge protectors temporarily.
• Inspect the cable and power adapter for bends, damage, looseness, or heat.
• Try another wall outlet.

4. Reboot the Roomba
• Hold the CLEAN button for about 20 seconds.
• Release it when the light ring changes/it restarts.
• Put it back on the dock and leave it for at least 3 hours.

5. Look for battery-age symptoms
• If it is several years old, the battery may charge only sometimes, report full then die quickly, or run for a very short time.
• A Roomba e5 battery is commonly due for replacement after roughly 2–3 years of regular use, sometimes sooner or later depending on use and storage conditions.
• Prefer an iRobot/OEM or reputable replacement battery; avoid damaged, swollen, or cheap unbranded packs.

6. Reseat the battery if needed
• If the above does not help, remove the battery following the e5 battery-replacement instructions, inspect for corrosion or swelling, and reseat it firmly.
• Do not reuse a swollen battery—replace it and contact iRobot support if there is any sign of overheating or leakage.

Most likely diagnosis:
• Charges when repositioned / pressure helps: dirty, worn, or stuck dock contacts.
• Dock has inconsistent power: outlet, adapter, or Home Base issue.
• Says charging but dies quickly or won’t hold charge: battery is likely failing.
• Still intermittent after cleaning, rebooting, and testing another outlet: Home Base contact assembly or the robot’s charging circuitry may need repair/replacement.

If you can share what the light ring/app says when it fails, and whether pressing it into the dock makes charging start, that would narrow it down quickly.
App says 'Charging error 5', ring is red and it does a two-tone sound. Fine if I wiggle it on the dock. No heat or smell from it.

“Charging error 5” on a Roomba e5 indicates a charging-system fault. Since it starts charging when you wiggle it on the dock, the most likely cause is intermittent contact between the robot and Home Base, rather than overheating or an immediate battery safety issue.

Try this:

1. Unplug the Home Base from the wall.
2. Clean all four charging contacts
• Two large metal pads underneath the Roomba.
• Two metal/spring contacts on the dock.
• Use a microfiber cloth. If dirty or dull, use a little 70%+ isopropyl alcohol, then allow to dry completely.
3. Check the dock pins
• Press each dock contact gently several times. Both should spring up evenly and not stick, feel loose, or sit lower than the other.
• Look for corrosion, pitting, black marks, or a bent contact.
4. Check the Roomba’s contact pads
• They should be reasonably flat and clean, not heavily scratched, burned, or recessed.
5. Put the dock on a hard, level floor, plugged directly into a wall outlet, and manually place the Roomba onto it. Make sure it is centered.

If it only charges when you press/wiggle it, watch which direction makes it work:
• Pushing it toward the dock helps: likely dirty/worn contacts or weak/sticking dock springs.
• Lifting one side or shifting sideways helps: dock may be uneven, contacts may be worn, or the robot’s underside/contact assembly may be misaligned.

You can also reboot it after cleaning:
• Hold CLEAN for about 20 seconds, release, let it restart, then dock it again.

Because Error 5 can also be caused by an internal charging/battery fault, if thoroughly cleaned contacts and freely moving dock pins do not solve it, the next likely parts are the Home Base/power supply or the Roomba battery/contact/charging circuitry. Given the wiggle symptom, I’d investigate or replace the Home Base first before replacing the battery—unless the battery is old and runtime has also become very short.

Until it is reliable, don’t leave it charging unattended for long periods. No heat, swelling, or smell is reassuring, but stop using/charging it if any of those appear.

I cleaned the contacts. They were dull with a greasy grey film, plus lots of hair on the robot ones. They're silver underneath and the dock ones spring up and down fine. It's charged every night for 4 days since, no error. Not sure which way the wiggle goes.

That strongly points to dirty charging contacts being the cause. The greasy grey film and hair can create enough resistance that the Roomba intermittently fails to detect or maintain charging, producing Error 5. The fact it has charged normally for four consecutive nights after cleaning is a very good sign.

A few practical steps:

• Keep the Home Base on a hard, flat surface and leave some clear space around it so the robot docks consistently.
• Every month or two, wipe the robot and dock charging contacts with a dry cloth; use a little isopropyl alcohol only if they start looking dull/greasy again.
• Remove hair buildup around the underside and front wheel/caster area, since it can affect how squarely the robot sits on the dock.
• If Error 5 returns, first inspect whether one dock contact is sticking or whether the pads have become dirty again.

You probably do not need a battery or dock replacement at this point. If it goes another week or two without errors and has normal runtime, treat the cleaning as the fix.
